question.text: Gulfstream Global Partners, a Singapore-tax-resident LP of a Cat II AIF, is about to claim India-Singapore treaty benefits on capital gains. The Multilateral Instrument (MLI) introduces a 'Principal Purpose Test' (PPT) into the treaty. What is the effect of the PPT?

answer.text: Treaty benefits are denied if obtaining the benefit was one of the principal purposes of the arrangement, unless granting the benefit is in accordance with the object and purpose of the treaty.
Treaty benefits are automatically available to all Singapore residents.
PPT only applies to dividend income, not to capital gains.
PPT replaces GAAR entirely — GAAR no longer applies once MLI is in force.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Under the MLI (signed by India on 7 June 2017, ratified on 25 June 2019, in force from 1 October 2019), the PPT (BEPS Action 6) denies treaty benefits if it is reasonable to conclude that obtaining the benefit was ONE of the principal purposes of the arrangement — unless granting the benefit is consistent with the treaty's object and purpose. Many Indian treaties (including India-Singapore) also have a Limitation of Benefit (LOB) clause. PPT is an OVERLAY, not a replacement for GAAR. **The Trap:** Option B ignores the entire anti-abuse framework. Option C narrows PPT to dividends only — it applies across the treaty. Option D wrongly claims PPT replaces GAAR; both operate in parallel and CBDT guidance confirms this. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests MLI/PPT/LOB as part of the treaty-interpretation toolkit. X-B (IA L2) tests it for HNI cross-border planning. XV (RA) touches on it for issuer-residency analysis. Indian treaties with Mauritius and Singapore were renegotiated (2016-17) to grandfather pre-2017 investments, now layered with MLI-PPT. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Before accepting a foreign LP into your Cat II fund, run a PPT stress-test on their routing: does the LP entity have genuine substance in the treaty jurisdiction (employees, office, board meetings, decision-making)? A pure letterbox SPV will fail PPT and expose both the LP and your fund to reassessment risk.
